label: lem:adelic-corrected-frames
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The formulas \begin{equation} T_g=q(A_g)^{-1}D_g,\qquad W_g=q(\beta_g)^{-1}D_g\qquad(g\in M_0) \label{eq:adelic-corrected-frames} \end{equation} define continuous homomorphisms $T:M_0\to N_3(4)$ and $W:M_0\to N_4(4)$.

label: lem:adelic-kernel-normality
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint kernel of $T,W$ in $M_0$ is normal in $\mathcal G$.

label: prop:adelic-cm-images
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full division fields are \[ \mathbb Q(E_j[\mathrm{tors}])=K_j^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] On $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, one has \begin{equation} \rho_4(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=N_4(4),\qquad \rho_3^{\circ}(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=N_3(4),\qquad \rho_3^{\circ}=\kappa\rho_3. \label{eq:adelic-arithmetic-projections} \end{equation} The representations $\rho_3^{\circ}$ and $\rho_3$ have the same kernel on $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$.

label: lem:adelic-cm-entanglement
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The intersection of the two full division fields is \begin{equation} K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}\cap K_4^{\mathrm{ab}} =\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}(3^{1/4}). \label{eq:adelic-cm-intersection} \end{equation} In the representations of Proposition~\ref{prop:adelic-cm-images}, the joint image of $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ is exactly $\mathcal E$.

label: prop:adelic-signed-path-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Choose the Tate-module bases by transport along paths to the harmonic and equianharmonic fibres of the Legendre family. For $\sigma\in H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ one then has the exact integral identities \begin{equation} W_\sigma=\rho_4(\sigma),\qquad T_\sigma=\rho_3^{\circ}(\sigma) =\kappa(\sigma)\rho_3(\sigma). \label{eq:adelic-signed-path-comparison} \end{equation} In particular $(T,W)(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=\mathcal E$.

label: thm:adelic-frame-elimination
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $G_1=G\cap M_0$. Then \begin{equation} (T,W)(G_1)=(T,W)(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=\mathcal E. \label{eq:adelic-gt-arithmetic-image} \end{equation} In particular, the closed normal subgroup \begin{equation} C_{\mathrm{CM}}= \ker\bigl((T,W):G_1\longrightarrow N_3(4)\times N_4(4)\bigr) \label{eq:adelic-cm-kernel} \end{equation} satisfies \begin{equation} G=C_{\mathrm{CM}}H,\qquad C_{\mathrm{CM}}\cap H= G_{K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}}. \label{eq:adelic-cm-normalization} \end{equation} The inclusion of $H$ induces the canonical isomorphism \begin{equation} G/C_{\mathrm{CM}}\simeq \operatorname{Gal}(K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}/\mathbb Q). \label{eq:adelic-cm-arithmetic-quotient} \end{equation} Every continuous abelian character of $G$ that is zero on $H$ and whose restriction to $G_1$ factors through $(T,W)$ is zero.

label: prop:arithmetic-affine
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroup $N$ is closed and normal in $G$, and $N\cap H=K$. The map $(\lambda,\rho _2)$ identifies $G/N$ with \[ A=\{(a,r)\in U\ltimes\widehat{\mathbb Z}: r\bmod 2=\epsilon _8(a)\}, \qquad (a,r)(b,s)=(ab,r+as). \] This identifies $G/N$ canonically with $\operatorname{Gal}(K_2/\mathbb Q)$. In particular $\rho _2\bmod 2=\epsilon _8\circ\lambda$ on $G$.

label: prop:arithmetic-commutators
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $T=\{(1,2t):t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\}\subset A$. Then \[ \overline{[A,A]}=T,\qquad \overline{[A,T]}=\{(1,4t):t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\}. \] Every finite $p$-group quotient of $A$ is abelian when $p$ is odd. Every finite quotient of $A$ which is a $2$-group of nilpotency class at most two has commutator subgroup of order at most two.

label: lem:character-gluing
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $G=NH$ be a profinite group with $N$ closed and normal and $H$ closed, and put $K=N\cap H$. Let $M$ be a finite abelian group with trivial action. An invariant character $\psi:N\to M$ and a character $\eta:H\to M$ extend to a character of $G$ if and only if $\psi|_K=\eta|_K$. The extension is unique and is given by \[ \chi(nh)=\psi(n)+\eta(h). \]

label: thm:abelian-splitting
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of profinite abelian groups \[ G^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq U\times B \] under which the multiplier is the first projection. Moreover \[ C_N=N\cap\overline{[G,G]},\qquad B\simeq\bigl(G/\overline{\langle\!\langle H\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr)^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p=H^1(N,\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad r_p:X_p\longrightarrow H^1(K,\mathbb F_p). \] Restriction gives canonical identifications \begin{align*} \ker r_p&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p),\\ H^1(G,\mathbb F_p)&\simeq \lambda^*H^1(U,\mathbb F_p)\oplus\ker r_p. \end{align*} Consequently $\ker r_p=0$ if and only if every continuous $\mathbb F_p$-character of $G$ factors through the multiplier. The multiplier identifies $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $U$ if and only if $N\subset\overline{[G,G]}$, and this holds if and only if $\ker r_p=0$ for every prime~$p$.

label: prop:transgression-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The transgression $d_H:Y_p\to H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)$ is injective and identifies $Y_p$ with \[ \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)\longrightarrow H^2(H,\mathbb F_p)\bigr). \] There is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p) \longrightarrow X_p \xrightarrow{\ d_Hr_p\ } \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)\longrightarrow H^2(G,\mathbb F_p)\bigr) \longrightarrow0. \] Thus, under the injection $d_H$, the image of restriction is precisely the inflation kernel for~$G$.

label: thm:arithmetic-target-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p$, \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_p}H^1(G_{K_2},\mathbb F_p)^{G_{\mathbb Q}}=\aleph_0. \] For $p=2$, an explicit independent family is given, for the odd rational primes $q$, by the quadratic extensions $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$. Equivalently these are the Kummer classes of $\sqrt q$ in $K_2^\times/(K_2^\times)^2$.

label: lem:ihara-cocycle
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g,g'\in\GTz$, \[ \rho_d^I(gg')=\rho_d^I(g)+\lambda(g)\rho_d^I(g'). \] If $n\in N$, then \[ \rho_d^I(gng^{-1})=\lambda(g)\rho_d^I(n). \]

label: lem:cyclic-cover-symmetry
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $F=\widehat F_2=\langle x,y\rangle$. Suppose a continuous automorphism $\phi$ satisfies \[ \phi(x)=x,\qquad \phi(y)=f^{-1}yf,\qquad f\in\overline{[F,F]}, \] and $\phi(xy)$ is conjugate to $xy$. For a positive integer $n$, use the free basis \[ X=x^n,\qquad Y_j=x^jyx^{-j}\quad(0\leq j<n) \] of $H_n$. If $[f]=a[X]+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j[Y_j]$ in $H_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$, then \[ a=0,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j=0,\qquad c_j=c_{-j\bmod n}\quad(0\leq j<n). \]

label: thm:all-kummer-parity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every positive integer $d$, Ihara's integral Kummer cocycle is even on the multiplier-one subgroup of the gentle group: \[ \rho_d^I\bigl(\ker(\lambda:\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\to U)\bigr) \subset2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] On the whole gentle group it satisfies \[ \rho_d^I\bmod2=\epsilon_d\circ\lambda, \] where $\epsilon_d:U\to\mathbb F_2$ is the additive quadratic Dirichlet character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$.

label: thm:quadratic-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The vector space of invariant continuous quadratic characters of the normalized subgroup has dimension \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(\Lambda_0,\mathbb F_2)^{\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}} =\aleph_0. \] For every positive integer $d$ the formula \[ \psi_d^N=\frac{\rho_d^I|_N}{2}\bmod2 \] defines a continuous invariant quadratic character. For the odd rational primes $q$, the characters $\psi_q^N$ are linearly independent and restrict to the characters of $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$. Thus \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{im}r_2=\aleph_0. \] More precisely, for distinct odd primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, let $R:N\to\mathbb Z_2^m$ be the vector of the $2$-adic components of $\rho_{q_1}^I,\ldots,\rho_{q_m}^I$. Then \[ R(K)=R(N)=2\mathbb Z_2^m, \] and restriction is injective on the $m$-dimensional character space obtained by pullback from this lattice.

label: lem:integral-alternating-cubic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $f$ be a pro-$2$ commutator word satisfying \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Set $a=[S^2T]f$ and $A=[S^2T^2S]f$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:alternating-cubic-identity} [STS]f=-2a,\qquad [ST^2S]f=a,\qquad [STSTS]f=-2a-4A. \end{equation} In particular, $[STSTS]f\equiv2a\pmod4$.

label: prop:cubic-magnus-eight
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently \[ \eta_3:N\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_3(g)=m_3(g)/8\pmod2 \] is an ordinary continuous $G$-invariant quadratic character.

label: lem:rho2-cubic-modfour
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every multiplier-one gentle element, \[ \rho_2^I(g)\equiv-2m_3(g)\pmod4 \] in the $2$-adic coordinate.

label: prop:cubic-arithmetic-witness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists $k\in K_{\mathrm{rad}}$ such that \[ m_3(k)\in8\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] In particular, $\eta_3|_{K_{\mathrm{rad}}}\ne0$, so $\eta_3$ is independent of every character generated by rational Kummer coordinates. Moreover, \[ m_3(D)=m_3(K_{\mathrm{rad}})=8\mathbf Z_2. \]

label: cor:cubic-radical-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Define \[ D_3=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}=D\cap\ker m_3, \qquad K_{\mathrm{rad},3}=K_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\ker m_3. \] Then $D_3$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, and \[ D=D_3K_{\mathrm{rad}},\qquad G=D_3H,\qquad D_3\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad},3}. \] Writing \[ B=N/\overline{[G,N]K},\qquad K=N\cap H, \] the previously obtained radical normalization refines canonically to \[ B\simeq D/\overline{[G,D]K_{\mathrm{rad}}} \simeq D_3/\overline{[G,D_3]K_{\mathrm{rad},3}}. \] If $L_3=\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\,K_{\mathrm{rad},3}}$, then $\operatorname{Gal}(L_3/L)\simeq\mathbf Z_2$. This defines the arithmetic extension by the explicit cubic monodromy coordinate; no radical formula for $L_3$ is asserted.

label: cor:cubic-radical-joint-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\widehat{\mathbf Z}\right) \times8\mathbf Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)) \] has kernel $D_3$ and is surjective; already its restriction to $K=N\cap H$ is surjective. Consequently the $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-characters of $N$ which vanish on $D_3$ form exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero $G$-invariant $\mathbf F_p$-character of $N$ vanishes on $D_3$.

label: lem:cubic-branch-filling
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f_g)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Fill the punctures $0,\infty$ in the threefold cyclic cover $\mathbb P^1_t\setminus\{0,\infty,1,\omega,\omega^2\}$. The restriction of the standard action $\phi_g$ on the base group, followed by this filling, induces on $\pi_1(\mathbb P^1_t\setminus\{1,\omega,\omega^2\})$ the outer class of the same $g$.

label: prop:normalized-HF1-from-normalizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $g=(1,f_g)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ and $\rho_3^I(g)=0$, then its pure cubic conjugator satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-normalizer-13} \boxed{\quad A_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uv)\quad} \end{equation} in the full signed profinite braid group.

label: cor:cubic-defect-zero-normalizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$ the finite cubic comparison defect $\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$ vanishes. Together with the harmonic comparison, this gives $\chi_3=0$ on full GT.

label: lem:eighth-two-conductor
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $n=2,4,8$, the field $L_n=\mathbb Q(i,2^{1/n})$ is cyclic of degree $n$ over $K_4$. Its conductor is respectively $\mathfrak p^4,\mathfrak p^6,\mathfrak p^8$. In particular \[ L_4\subset K_4(E_4[8]),\qquad L_8\subset K_4(E_4[16]). \]

label: prop:eighth-two-division-fields
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $k=\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}$ one has \[ k(E_4[8])=k(2^{1/4}),\qquad k(E_4[16])=k(2^{1/8}). \]

label: lem:eighth-two-class-two-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Modulo sixteen the commutator subgroup of $q(F)$ is the central cyclic group of order four generated by \[ C=[U^2,L^2] =\begin{pmatrix}13&8\\8&5\end{pmatrix}\pmod{16}. \] In particular $q_{16}(\gamma_3F)=1$.

label: lem:eighth-two-normalized-gentle
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $h=(1,f)$ is gentle and $\rho_2(h)=0$, then \[ \beta_h\in\gamma_3F,\qquad q_{16}(\beta_h)=D_h\bmod16=W_h\bmod16=I. \]

label: thm:eighth-two-compatibility
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement:
Let $M_0=\ker\lambda$ in the gentle group. Define the continuous homomorphism $
u_2:N_4(4)	o\mathbb Z/4$ by its arithmetic normalization: \[ 
u_2(ho_4(\sigma)) = rac{\kappa_2(\sigma)}2\pmod4 \qquad(\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}}). \] This is well defined and has kernel the subgroup congruent to one modulo sixteen. For every $h\in M_0$,  egin{equation} 
u_2(W_h)= rac{ho_2(h)}2\pmod4. \label{eq:eighth-two-frame-kummer} \end{equation} In particular the exceptional eighth-root coordinate of $2$ in the radical--CM compatibility defect is identically zero on full GT.

label: lem:cubic-two-pure-frame
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $h\in M_0$, one has $A_h\in F'$.

label: prop:cubic-two-compatibility
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $h\in M_0$, \[ j_3(T_h)=\rho_2(h)\pmod3. \] On the arithmetic subgroup, this quotient is the Kummer action on $k(2^{1/3})/k$, with the indicated choice of exponent.

label: cor:complete-two-compatibility
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement:
There is a continuous homomorphism \[ 
u_{2,\mathrm{CM}}:N_3(4)	imes N_4(4) \longrightarrow\mathbb Z/12 \] specified by \[ 
u_{2,\mathrm{CM}}(t,w)\equiv
u_2(w)\pmod4,\qquad 
u_{2,\mathrm{CM}}(t,w)\equiv2j_3(t)\pmod3 . \] For every $h\in M_0$, \[ 
u_{2,\mathrm{CM}}(T_h,W_h)= rac{ho_2(h)}2\pmod{12}. \] Arithmetically this is the common quotient $\operatorname{Gal}(k(2^{1/24})/k)$, with Kummer exponent $\kappa_2/2$. In particular the entire order-twelve coordinate belonging to $2$ in the radical--CM compatibility defect vanishes on full GT.

label: lem:kn-different-local-systems
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $n=11$ and a primitive cube root $\omega$ in $\mathbb F_{17^2}$, consider characters over $\overline{\mathbb F}_{17}$. The character of $H_{11}$ obtained by pulling back $x\mapsto1,y\mapsto\omega$ along $d_{11}$ is different from the restriction of every character $x\mapsto\xi,y\mapsto\omega$ with $\xi^{11}=1$. Nor is either kind a deck translate of the other.

label: prop:kn-linear-sign-model
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an $\mathbb F_{17}$-linear automorphism of the space \eqref{eq:eleventh-local-system-H} that commutes with the whole deck group $A$, preserves its alternating intersection form, and has determinant $-1$ on the ten-dimensional $\omega$-eigenspace over $\mathbb F_{17^2}$. Its quadratic norm-one determinant sign is therefore $-1$. This is a linear model, not a GT element or a solution of the pentagon or of \eqref{eq:eleventh-local-system-K}.

label: prop:eta-ten-no-extension-d7
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_{10}$ on $D_9$ extends invariantly to $D_8$ by $\alpha_{10}$, but has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_7$. Consequently it has no such extension to $D_5$, $D_3$, $D$ or $N$.

label: cor:weight-ten-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic-character kernels on restriction to $D_{10}$ are \[ \begin{array}{c|l} \text{domain}&\text{kernel}\\ \hline D_9&\mathbf F_2\eta_{10}\\ D_8&\mathbf F_2\eta_9\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_{10}\\ D_7&\mathbf F_2\eta_8\oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_5&\mathbf F_2\eta_7\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_8\\ D_3&\mathbf F_2\eta_5\\ N&\displaystyle\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \end{array} \]

label: prop:eta-eight-no-extension-d3
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_8$ on $D_7$ extends to the invariant character \[ \alpha_8:D_5\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2,\qquad \alpha_8(1,f)=[S^4TST^2]f\pmod2, \] but has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_3$. More precisely, no nonzero linear combination of $\eta_7$ and $\alpha_8$ on $D_5$ extends to a $G$-invariant character of $D_3$.

label: cor:d3-character-kernel-d8
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(D_3,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\mathbf F_2)\right) =\mathbf F_2\eta_5. \]

label: prop:finite-interchange
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $X=U^2\bmod8$ and $P=\langle X,R\bmod8\rangle\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/8)$. There is a surjection \[ \kappa:P\longrightarrow\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3) \] such that \[ \kappa(X)=-S\bmod3,\qquad \kappa(R)=U\bmod3,\qquad \kappa(5I)=-I. \] The group $P$ has order $192$ and the kernel has order eight. For every profinite commutator word $f\in\widehat F(x,y)'$, \[ \kappa\bigl(f(X,R)\bigr)=f(S,U)=f(U,S)^{-1} \] if $f$ satisfies the two-cycle relation.

label: lem:common-sign
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$ the matrix $f_g(U,S)\bmod3$ is central. Consequently \[ f_g(U,S)=(-I)^{\eta(g)}\quad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3) \] defines a continuous homomorphism $\eta:D\to\mathbb F_2$.

label: prop:pair-of-gates
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in D$ define \[ \epsilon_h(g)=w(g)+\eta(g),\qquad \epsilon_c(g)=\tau(g)+\eta(g). \] These are continuous homomorphisms on $D$, and \[ \boxed{\quad \chi_3=\epsilon_h+\epsilon_c.\quad} \] More explicitly, the two signs are the following finite defects: \[ \begin{split} (-I)^{\epsilon_h(g)} &=q_3(\beta_g)^{-1}f_g(U,S)^{-1},\\ (-I)^{\epsilon_c(g)} &=\kappa\!\left(q_8(A_g)^{-1}f_g(X,R)^{-1}\right). \end{split} \] In particular the two finite comparisons \begin{equation} q_3(\beta_g)^{-1}=f_g(U,S),\qquad \kappa(q_8(A_g)^{-1})=\kappa(f_g(X,R)) \label{eq:finite-harmonic-cubic-comparisons} \end{equation} would imply $\chi_3(g)=0$. They are sufficient conditions; vanishing of $\chi_3$ requires only equality of their two defects. Both defects vanish on $D\cap G_{\mathbb Q}$.

label: lem:eta-quotient-invariant
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The kernel of the evaluation \[ e:\widehat F(x,y)\longrightarrow Q=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3), \qquad e(x)=U,\quad e(y)=S, \] is invariant under every gentle automorphism. Consequently $\eta$ is invariant under conjugation by all of $G$.

label: prop:two-relative-extensions
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Each of $\epsilon_h,\epsilon_c$ has a unique extension to a continuous homomorphism $G\to\mathbb F_2$ that is zero on $H$. Their sum is the established residual relative character $\chi_3$. The harmonic extension is proved to vanish in Section~\ref{sec:harmonic-dyadic-comparison}. The cubic extension and $\chi_3$ vanish by Section~\ref{sec:normalized-cubic-identity}.

label: prop:truncated-counterexample
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: In the mod-two Magnus ring $\mathcal R=\mathbb F_2\langle A,B\rangle/(\text{degree}\ge5)$, send $a$ to $1+A$ and $b$ to $1+B$. The word $\beta=a^3bab^3$ has exponent sums $(4,4)$ and satisfies \[ d\alpha(d)\alpha^2(d)=1\quad\text{in }\mathcal R. \] Nevertheless its image under $a\mapsto i,b\mapsto j$ in the quaternion group is $-1$. Thus this truncated norm equation and the two exponent sums modulo four do not determine the quaternion central sign.

label: lem:frame-all-multipliers-congruence
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in\mathcal G$ and every prime $\ell$ there is a unique matrix \[ D_{g,\ell}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{g,\ell}&b_{g,\ell}\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \] such that $\widetilde q_\ell\Phi_g=\operatorname{Ad}(D_{g,\ell})\widetilde q_\ell$. It depends continuously on $g$, and $D_{gh,\ell}=D_{g,\ell}D_{h,\ell}$. For $h\in N_0$, its reduction modulo twelve is the identity.

label: prop:frame-sign-conjugation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The restrictions of $a_2,a_3$, and hence $\delta$, to $N_0$ are invariant under conjugation by $\mathcal G$.

label: thm:global-frame-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a unique continuous character \[ \Delta:\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which restricts to $\delta$ on $N_0$ and is zero on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For any $g\in\mathcal G$, choose $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ with $(\lambda,\rho_2)(\sigma)=(\lambda,\rho_2)(g)$. Then \[ \Delta(g)=\delta(g\sigma^{-1}). \] This character vanishes on the full pentagon group.

label: prop:genus-two-finite-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a surjection \[ \ell:G_8\longrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3),\qquad U\longmapsto A,\quad R\longmapsto T, \] whose kernel is the order-eight subgroup \[ K=\langle Z,X^2C,Y^2C\rangle. \] It kills $Z$, so the signed congruence representation induces \[ \bar\ell:\Gamma=C_2*C_3\longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3). \] For $s=uvu$, $r=uv$ and $u=r^{-1}s$, their images have orders $2,3,8$, respectively. On the subgroup $P$, this map agrees with the previous interchange map on all commutator prowords in $X,R$, although its value on $X$ is $S$ instead of $-S$.

label: cor:genus-two-sign-cover
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The discrete kernel of $\bar\ell$ is the fundamental group of a genus-two surface with six punctures. Its compactification carries a faithful deck action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3)$ of signature $(2,3,8)$. The central involution is its hyperelliptic involution. On $D$ the induced action on this finite deck group is the identity. The pure harmonic conjugator maps to $I$, and the pure cubic conjugator maps to $(-I)^{\tau(g)}$.

label: lem:dyadic-branch-word
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $h(a,b)=f^+(a,1,b)$. Then \[ f(a,b)=h(a,b)h(b,a)^{-1} \quad\text{in }\widehat F(a,b). \]

label: lem:unique-swap-frame
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\gamma\mapsto\theta(\gamma)\gamma^{-1}$ on $\widehat F(a,b)$ is injective. In particular \[ \beta(a,b)=h(b,a). \]

label: prop:normalized-GF1-from-dyadic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g$ as above, in the full signed profinite braid group on generators $u,v$, with $s=uvu$, one has \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,s). \tag{GF1$_0$} \]

label: cor:harmonic-defect-zero
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$, the finite harmonic frame sign satisfies $w=\eta$. Thus the previously constructed relative character $\epsilon_h=w+\eta$ is zero on the whole of full GT, and the remaining exceptional character is $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$. The cubic comparison in Section~\ref{sec:normalized-cubic-identity} will also make this character zero.

label: thm:individual-frame-kummer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2)\subset\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, \[ a_2(g)=a_3(g)=\frac{\rho_3^I(g)}2\pmod2. \] In particular the character $a_2+\rho_3^I/2\bmod2$ is zero on $N$. Both frame signs vanish on the simultaneous radical-normalized subgroup $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$.

label: lem:iii-prime-two-dimensional
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $\rho:B_4\to\mathrm{GL}_2(k)$ be a homomorphism. Then $\rho((ab)^3)$ and $\rho((bc)^3)$ commute. For a finite field $k$ and $g\in D$, it follows that \[ g_g\bigl(\rho((ab)^3),\rho((bc)^3)\bigr)=1. \] Thus such a direct matrix specialization of $(\mathrm{III}')$ does not retain its harmonic auxiliary-word term.

label: lem:integral-boundary-measure
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in N$ there is an integral $\mathbf Z_2$-valued measure $\nu_{g,+}$ on $1+4\mathbf Z_2$, of total mass zero, such that \begin{equation} \int t^{2k}\,d\nu_{g,+}(t) =(1-2^{2k})\tau_{2k+1}(g)\qquad(k\ge1), \label{eq:integral-boundary-moments} \end{equation} where the normalization is exactly \[ c_{2k+1}(g)=[u^{2k}]q_g(e^u),\qquad \tau_{2k+1}(g)=\frac{(2k)!}{2}c_{2k+1}(g). \] The same formula defines an integral continuous homomorphism $\tau_{2k+1}:M\to\mathbf Z_2$ with conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2k+1}$. Its value modulo two is independent of $k$: \[ \tau_{2k+1}(g)\equiv\tau_3(g)=a_2(g)\pmod2 \qquad(g\in M). \]

label: lem:uniform-odd-coordinate-bound
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $g\in N$ and $a_2(g)=a_4(g)=\cdots=a_{2r-2}(g)=0$, then \[ a_{2r}(g)\in2^{2r+1}\mathbf Z_2. \]

label: prop:kummer-multiplicativity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For positive integers $a,b$ and every $g\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, \[ \rho_{ab}^I(g)=\rho_a^I(g)+\rho_b^I(g). \] Consequently \[ \rho_n^I=\sum_{q\mid n}v_q(n)\rho_q^I, \qquad \frac{\rho_{ab}^I-\rho_a^I-\rho_b^I}{2}\bmod2=0. \] The last expression therefore supplies no nonzero character in the restriction kernel.

label: cor:dyadic-anderson
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ satisfies all dyadic Anderson multiplication relations $(A_{2^j})$, $j\geq1$, in the notation of \cite[Definition 2.3]{Furusho2003}.

label: thm:main-structural
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Assume \eqref{eq:decomposition} and the preceding normalization of $\rho_2$. Then $N$ is closed and normal, $N\cap H=K$, and \[ \GT/N\simeq A:=\Gal(K_2/\Q). \] In the affine coordinates $(u,t)$, with product $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$, this quotient is \[ A=\{(u,t)\in\Zh^\times\ltimes\Zh: t\equiv\varepsilon_8(u)\pmod2\}, \] where $\varepsilon_8(u)=0$ for $u\equiv1,7\pmod8$ and $1$ for $u\equiv3,5\pmod8$. There is a canonical topological isomorphism \[ \GT^{\ab}\simeq\Zh^\times\times B,\qquad B=N/\overline{[\GT,N]K}. \] For every prime $p$, restriction identifies \[ \Hom(B,\F_p)\simeq\ker(X_p\longrightarrow Y_p). \] Consequently the relative kernel vanishes for every prime if and only if the multiplier identifies $\GT^{\ab}$ with $\Zh^\times$.

label: thm:main-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With the same notation, \[ \dim_{\F_2} X_2=\dim_{\F_2}\operatorname{im}(X_2\longrightarrow Y_2)=\aleph_0. \] For every positive integer $d$, Ihara's integral cocycle $\rho_d^I$ is even on the multiplier-one subgroup of $\GTz$. For every odd prime $q$, \[ \psi_q=\frac{\rho_q^I|_N}{2}\pmod2 \] is an invariant continuous character of $N$. Its restriction is the character of $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$, and these restrictions are linearly independent as $q$ varies. For every prime $p$, including odd $p$, $\dim_{\F_p}Y_p=\aleph_0$.

label: thm:main-rational-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With the preceding assumptions and notation, the joint map \[ N\longrightarrow\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh, \qquad n\longmapsto(\rho_q^I(n))_q \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, and \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad}}\GQ,\qquad N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\GQ=G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}},\qquad \GT/N_{\mathrm{rad}}\simeq\Gal(L_{\mathrm{rad}}/\Q). \] The latter quotient consists of the affine coordinates $(u,(t_q)_{q\text{ prime}})$ satisfying $t_q\equiv\epsilon_q(u)\pmod2$, with multiplication $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$; here $\epsilon_q$ is the character of $\Q(\sqrt q)$. The relative abelian quotient is unchanged: \[ B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}}. \] The invariant quadratic characters of $N$ that factor through all rational Kummer coordinates are exactly the finite linear combinations of the $\psi_q$ for odd primes $q$, and restriction is injective on this entire subspace. No nonzero invariant character with values in $\F_p$, for odd $p$, factors through these coordinates.

label: thm:main-congruence-frames
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f)\in\GT$ satisfy $\rho_2(g)=0$, and put \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}. \] In the signed adelic braid representation, \[ f(U^2,V^2)=I\quad\text{in }\operatorname{SL}_2(\Zh). \] For the signed cubic and harmonic frame bits $a_3(g),a_2(g)$ of \cite[Lemmas 12--15]{H17}, with the positive signed lifts specified in Section~\ref{sec:global-frame-character}, one has \[ a_2(g)=a_3(g)=\rho_3^I(g)/2\pmod2. \] In particular both signs vanish on $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$.

label: thm:main-cubic-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g=(1,f)$ put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f$ in the Magnus expansion $x=1+S$, $y=1+T$. Then \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\Z_2,\qquad m_3(N_{\mathrm{rad}})=m_3(G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}})=8\Z_2. \] Thus $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ belongs to $X_2$, and its restriction to $G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}$ is nonzero. It is linearly independent of the entire rational Kummer subspace. The joint map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh\right)\times8\Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto\bigl((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)\bigr) \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\ker m_3$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and of $\GT$, and \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad},3},\F_2)$ is precisely \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\F_2\eta_3. \] On $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$ put $m_5(g)=[S^4T]f$ and $K_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ$. Then \[ m_5(N_{\mathrm{rad},3})=m_5(K_{\mathrm{rad},3})=32\Z_2. \] Thus $N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\ker m_5$ is again proper and closed normal, with \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\cap\GQ)}. \] The divided character $\eta_5=m_5/32\pmod2$ on $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$ does not extend to an invariant quadratic character of $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or of $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5},\F_2)$ is still precisely the displayed rational Kummer and cubic span.

label: thm:main-weight-seven-alternative
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $D_3=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$, $D_5=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}$, and $J_5=D_5\cap H$. Every $g\in D_5$ starts in Magnus degree seven, and $m_7(g)=[S^6T]f_g$ is an additive weight-seven coordinate with \[ m_7(D_5)=m_7(J_5)=128\Z_2. \] The proper closed normal subgroup $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ satisfies \[ \GT=D_7H,\qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[\GT,D_7](D_7\cap H)}. \] The invariant character $\eta_7=m_7/128\pmod2$ on $D_5$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction. It has no invariant extension to $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_7,\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-weight-eight-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every $g\in D_7$ has Magnus expansion starting in degree at least eight. Put \[ m_8(g)=[S^4TST^2]f_g,\qquad J_7=D_7\cap H. \] This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^8$, and \[ m_8(D_7)=m_8(J_7)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_8$ is proper, closed and normal in $\GT$, satisfies $\GT=D_8H$, and gives \[ B\simeq D_8/\overline{[\GT,D_8](D_8\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_8$ starts in Magnus degree at least nine. The invariant quadratic character $\eta_8=m_8\pmod2$ on $D_7$ extends invariantly to $D_5$ by the same raw coefficient modulo two, but has no invariant extension to $D_3$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. More precisely, no nonzero combination of its extension and $\eta_7$ on $D_5$ extends invariantly to $D_3$, and \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(D_3,\F_2)^{\GT}\longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\F_2)\right) =\F_2\eta_5. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_8,\F_2)$ remains exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:main-weight-nine-bounds
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $J_j=D_j\cap H$ for $j=7,8$, and $m_9(g)=[S^8T]f_g$ for $g\in D_7$. This is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^9$, and \[ m_9(D_7)=m_9(J_7)=m_9(D_8)=m_9(J_8)=512\Z_2. \] Its integral kernel $D_9=D_8\cap\ker m_9$ is proper, closed and normal in $\GT$, and \[ \GT=D_9H,\qquad B\simeq D_9/\overline{[\GT,D_9](D_9\cap H)}. \] Every $D_9$ word starts in degree at least ten. The joint map $(m_8,m_9):D_7\to\Z_2\times512\Z_2$ is surjective already on $J_7$ and has kernel $D_9$. The invariant character $\eta_9=m_9/512\pmod2$ on $D_7$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction; its restriction to $D_8$ has no invariant extension to $D_5$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_9,\F_2)$ remains exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-weight-ten-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $D_9$, put $m_{10}(g)=[S^5TST^3]f_g$ and $J_9=D_9\cap H$. This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{10}$, with \[ m_{10}(D_9)=m_{10}(J_9)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_{10}$ is proper, closed and normal, and \[ \GT=D_{10}H,\qquad B\simeq D_{10}/\overline{[\GT,D_{10}](D_{10}\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_{10}$ starts in Magnus degree at least eleven. The invariant character $\eta_{10}=m_{10}\pmod2$ extends invariantly to $D_8$, but not to $D_7$ or any of $D_5,D_3,N_{\mathrm{rad}},N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_{10},\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-uniform-dyadic-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $C_0=D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and \[ C_r=D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker c_{2j+1},\qquad C_\infty=\bigcap_{r\ge0}C_r. \] For every $r\ge1$, the coefficient $m_{2r+1}=[S^{2r}T]f$ is additive on $C_{r-1}$, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, and satisfies \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1}\cap H) =2^{2r+1}\Z_2,\qquad \ker(m_{2r+1}|_{C_{r-1}})=C_r. \] All these subgroups are closed and normal, and \[ G=C_rH=C_\infty H,\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] The subgroup $C_\infty$ is exactly the kernel in $D$ of the dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(C_\infty,\F_2)$ is the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. Finally, $E=C_\infty\cap D_{10}$ has infinite index in $D_{10}$, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E](E\cap H)}. \] Its elements have no pro-$2$ Magnus term below degree eleven and have trivial dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E,\F_2)$ is again exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. The mixed coordinate $b_{11}=[S^6TST^3]f$ on $E$ is additive, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{11}$, and has full and arithmetic image $\Z_2$. Its kernel $E'$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, $G=E'H$, and \[ B\simeq E'/\overline{[G,E'](E'\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E',\F_2)$ is the same rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-cm-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The corrected pair $(T,W)$ has the same full adelic image on $G_1$ and on $G_{\Q^{\ab}}$. Its kernel $C_{\mathrm{CM}}$ in $G_1$ is closed and normal in $\GT$. If $K_3=\Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and $K_4=\Q(i)$, then \[ \GT=C_{\mathrm{CM}}\GQ,\qquad C_{\mathrm{CM}}\cap\GQ=G_{K_3^{\ab}K_4^{\ab}},\qquad \GT/C_{\mathrm{CM}}\simeq \Gal(K_3^{\ab}K_4^{\ab}/\Q). \] Every continuous abelian character of $\GT$ which is trivial on $\GQ$ and whose restriction to $G_1$ factors through $(T,W)$ is zero.

label: thm:main-harmonic-dyadic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_2(g)=0$, the pure harmonic frame satisfies \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uvu) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $w_3=\eta$ on $D$, the relative character $\epsilon_h$ is zero, and $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau_3+\eta$.

label: thm:main-cubic-normalized
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_3^I(g)=0$, the pure cubic frame satisfies \[ A_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uv) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $\epsilon_c=0$ and $\chi_3=0$ on full GT. The exceptional eighth-root-of-three compatibility is therefore satisfied. Joint radical--CM compatibility is equivalent to the remaining tame cubic and harmonic tests displayed above.

label: prop:normalized-congruence-triviality
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ satisfy $\rho_2(g)=0$. Then \[ f(U^2,V^2)=I \qquad\text{in }\operatorname{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \] Consequently $\widetilde q\Phi_g=\widetilde q$ on $\widehat B_3$.

label: lem:parabolic-centralizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The centralizer of $v$ in $\widehat B$ is $\overline{\langle v\rangle}\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, and it has trivial intersection with $\mathcal C$.

label: cor:level-three-exact-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For a normalized $g=(1,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, put $q=f(u^2,v^2)\in\widehat B$. The element $q$ lies in $\mathcal C$, hence in $\overline{\Gamma_0(3)}$. The automorphism $\Phi_g$ preserves that subgroup. For $d_3:\overline{\Gamma_0(3)}\to\widehat B$ induced by conjugation by $\operatorname{diag}(3,1)$, set \[ h_3=d_3(q)q^{-1}. \] Then $h_3\in\mathcal C$, and strict compatibility with both level-three degeneracy maps is equivalent to the exact identity \[ d_3(q)=q. \]

label: lem:all-finite-unitarity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose that $\lambda_g=1$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $a,b\in\overline{\mathbb F}_p^\times$ have finite orders prime to $p$. Then \[ B_g(a,b)B_g(a^{-1},b^{-1})=1. \] In fact $B_g(a,b)=1$ if $a=1$, $b=1$, or $ab=1$.

label: thm:odd-anderson-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $p\equiv5\pmod{12}$ be prime, and let $n\geq1$ satisfy $\gcd(n,3p)=1$. Choose a primitive cube root $\omega\in\mathbb F_{p^2}$. The expression \begin{equation} E_{p,n}(g)= \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}B_g(\omega,\omega^k)} {\displaystyle\prod_{\xi^n=1}B_g(\xi,\omega)} \label{eq:odd-anderson-defect} \end{equation} belongs to the norm-one subgroup of $\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times$. Here all evaluations are reduced modulo $p$, and the denominator ranges over all $n$th roots in $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$. The rule \begin{equation} (-1)^{\Theta_{p,n}(g)}=E_{p,n}(g)^{(p+1)/2} \label{eq:odd-anderson-sign} \end{equation} defines a continuous homomorphism $G_0\to\mathbb F_2$, independent of the choice between $\omega$ and $\omega^2$. It vanishes on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. In particular its restriction to $G$ is an explicit candidate for a nonzero element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G/\langle\!\langle G_{\mathbb Q}\rangle\!\rangle,\mathbb F_2)$. The theorem does not assert that this restriction is nonzero.

label: cor:concrete-radical-anderson-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $H=G_{\mathbb Q}$ and let $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ be the simultaneous kernel in $G$ of the multiplier and the rational-prime Kummer cocycles. Put \[ L_{\mathrm{rad}}=\mathbb Q(\mu_\infty,q^{1/m}: q\text{ prime},\ m\geq1), \qquad K_{\mathrm{rad}}=G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \] Assume the simultaneous normalization $G=N_{\mathrm{rad}}H$, with $N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and identify the relative abelian quotient as \[ B=N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[G,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]K_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \] For a primitive cube root $\omega\in\mathbb F_{289}$ the formula \begin{equation} (-1)^{\psi_{17,11}(u)}= \left(\prod_{\substack{\xi^{11}=1\\\xi\ne1}} B_u(\xi,\omega)\right)^9, \qquad u\in N_{\mathrm{rad}}, \label{eq:concrete-radical-anderson-sign} \end{equation} defines a continuous $G$-invariant quadratic character vanishing on $K_{\mathrm{rad}}$. It therefore gives a precisely specified element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_2)$. Its unique extension to $G$ vanishing on $H$ is $\Theta_{17,11}$. In particular $\psi_{17,11}$ is nonzero if and only if $\Theta_{17,11}|_G$ is nonzero; neither nonvanishing assertion is proved here.

label: prop:formal-odd-sign
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists a Frobenius-equivariant sign-valued formal gamma function at the prime $17$ whose beta coboundary satisfies beta associativity, symmetry, the unitary relation, and the duplication formula, but for which the expression in \eqref{eq:odd-anderson-gamma} with $n=11$ equals $-1$. It may be taken constant in the pro-$17$ directions, so all its logarithmic derivatives vanish. This is a non-implication statement for the listed formal identities. It does not provide a solution of the full nonabelian relations $(K_n)$ or of the pentagon equation.

label: thm:radical-cm-intersection
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \begin{align} L_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap L_{\mathrm{CM}} &=L_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap F_{12}^{\mathrm{ab}}\notag\\ &=k\bigl(q^{1/12}:q\in\mathcal P,\, 2^{1/8},3^{1/8}\bigr)=:I. \label{eq:radical-cm-intersection} \end{align} In particular \begin{equation} \operatorname{Gal}(I/k)\simeq (\mathbb Z/12)^2\times \prod_{q\in\mathcal P\setminus\{2,3\}}\mathbb Z/6. \label{eq:radical-cm-common-group} \end{equation} The first two factors are indexed by $2,3$. In these coordinates conjugation by an element of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ is multiplication by its cyclotomic character, reduced modulo the indicated orders.

label: prop:radical-cm-joint-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $G=(N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap C_{\mathrm{CM}})H$; \item the joint radical and CM image of $G$ equals that of $H$; \item $a=b$, or equivalently $d=0$. \end{enumerate} Thus the remaining compatibility has exponent dividing twelve over $k$: it consists of one cubic coordinate for every rational prime, one quadratic coordinate for each prime other than $2,3$, and one coordinate modulo four for each of $2,3$.

label: lem:simultaneous-kummer-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For distinct rational primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, the joint Kummer map \[ G_{\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}}\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}, \qquad \sigma\longmapsto (\kappa_{q_1}(\sigma),\ldots,\kappa_{q_m}(\sigma)) \] has image exactly $2\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}$. Consequently, for distinct odd primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, its restriction to $K=G_{K_2}$ also has image $2\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}$.

label: thm:rational-radical-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint map \[ \mathcal R:N\longrightarrow \prod_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}}2\widehat{\mathbb Z}, \qquad n\longmapsto(\rho_q^I(n))_q \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel is $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and \[ N=N_{\mathrm{rad}}K,\qquad G=N_{\mathrm{rad}}H,\qquad N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad}}. \] In particular $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $N$, and \[ N/N_{\mathrm{rad}}\simeq \prod_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}}2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] There are canonical topological isomorphisms \begin{align*} G/N_{\mathrm{rad}}&\simeq \operatorname{Gal}(L_{\mathrm{rad}}/\mathbb Q),\\ B&\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[G,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]K_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \end{align*} The first quotient is explicitly \[ A_{\mathrm{rad}}= \left\{(u,(t_q)_{q\in\mathcal P}): \begin{array}{l} u\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\quad t_q\in\widehat{\mathbb Z},\\ t_q\equiv\epsilon_q(u)\pmod2\quad(q\in\mathcal P) \end{array}\right\}, \] with multiplication $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$, where $\epsilon_q$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$.

label: cor:rational-kummer-characters
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic characters of $N$ that factor through all rational Kummer coordinates form exactly \[ X_2^{\mathrm{Kum}}= \bigoplus_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}} \mathbb F_2\,\psi_q^N. \] Restriction to $K$ is injective on this subspace. For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero invariant $\mathbb F_p$-character of $N$ factors through the rational Kummer coordinates. For every prime $p$, the unresolved relative kernel is equivalently \[ \operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathbb F_p)= \left\{\chi\in H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^G: \chi|_{K_{\mathrm{rad}}}=0\right\}. \]

label: prop:radical-character-pullback
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p^{\mathrm{rad}}=H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}=H^1(K_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^H. \] The restriction maps identify $X_p$ with the fiber product \[ X_p\simeq X_p^{\mathrm{rad}} \mathop{\times}_{Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}}Y_p. \] The kernels of $X_p\to X_p^{\mathrm{rad}}$ and $Y_p\to Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}$ are identified by restriction. They are zero for odd $p$, and for $p=2$ they are respectively $X_2^{\mathrm{Kum}}$ and its restriction to $K$.

label: prop:normalized-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a natural homeomorphism of right-coset spaces \[ N/K\longrightarrow G/H,\qquad nK\longmapsto nH. \] In particular $G=H$ if and only if $N=K$. Put $N_0=\ker(\lambda:\GTz\to U)\cap\ker\rho_2$. Then $\GTz=N_0H$. If a continuous homomorphism from $\GTz$ to any topological group is trivial on $H$, its restriction to $G$ is trivial if and only if its restriction to $N$ is trivial.

label: prop:lr-abstract-countermodel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Separate arithmetic quotient identifications do not imply vanishing of a cyclotomically crossed defect. Even a trivial ordinary relative abelian quotient does not force its order-three component to vanish.

label: prop:lr-integral-cubic-beta
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in N$, an integral identification of the quadratic orders identifies $T_g$ with either $(-1)^{a_2(g)}\nu_g$ or $(-1)^{a_2(g)}\overline{\nu_g}$. For $g\in D$ the sign is one. No uniform orientation is needed for cube membership or for the scalar modulo-eight bit.

label: lem:lr-cubic-cm-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The maximal exponent-three subextension of $K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}/k$ is $k(q^{1/3}:q\text{ rational prime})$. The order-three part of $d$ is therefore zero if and only if $T_g\in N_3(4)^3$ for every $g\in D$.

label: lem:lr-wild-three-cube
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$, the three-adic component of $\nu_g$ is a cube in the norm-one units of $\mathbb Z_3[\omega]$.

label: thm:lr-tame-cubic-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The order-three component of $d$ vanishes if and only if, for all $g\in D$ and primes $\ell\ge5$, \begin{equation} B_{g,\ell}(\omega,\omega)^{(\ell-\chi_{-3}(\ell))/3}=1 \quad\text{in the residue norm-one torus}. \label{eq:lr-tame-cubic-test} \end{equation} Use a primitive cube root in $\mathbb F_\ell$ in the split case and in $\mathbb F_{\ell^2}$ in the inert case.

label: prop:lr-formal-beta-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Beta associativity, unitarity, all dyadic Anderson identities, vanishing integral Kummer coordinates, and the logarithmic derivatives of the Anderson identities do not, as formal integral Alexander identities, imply all tests \eqref{eq:lr-tame-cubic-test}.

label: lem:lr-quartic-cm-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The maximal elementary-two subextension of $K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}/k$ is \[k(q^{1/4}:q\text{ rational prime}).\]

label: lem:lr-cubic-eight-field
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has $k(E_3[8])=k(\alpha,v)$. The scalar automorphism $[-1]$ of this division field fixes $v$. On $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, if \[ T_{\sigma,2}\equiv(1+4\tau(\sigma))I\pmod8, \qquad \tau(\sigma)\in\mathbb F_2, \] then $\sigma(v)/v=(-1)^{\tau(\sigma)}$.

label: prop:lr-exceptional-three-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\chi_3=w_3+\tau_3$ on $D$ is $G$-invariant and zero on $D\cap H$. It extends uniquely to an ordinary continuous quadratic character on $G$ that is zero on $H$. Its vanishing is exactly the remaining compatibility for $3^{1/8}$, once the known quartic coordinate of three is imposed. Moreover \[ \tau_3(g)=\frac{B_{g,2}(\omega,\omega)-1}{4}\pmod2, \] where the right side is scalar, in $\mathbb F_2\subset\mathbb F_4$.

label: prop:tame-harmonic-word-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$ the corrected harmonic frame satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-harmonic-1} W_g=f_g(U^2,S)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \end{equation} Consequently its residue belongs to the cyclic group \[ \mathcal T_\ell =\{aI+bS_\ell:a,b\in\mathbb F_\ell,\ a^2+b^2=1\}, \qquad |\mathcal T_\ell|=\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell). \] The simultaneous compatibility of the radical and CM actions on every rational quartic root is equivalent to the following family of finite word identities: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-harmonic-2} \boxed{\quad f_g(U_\ell^2,S_\ell)^{m_\ell}=I \qquad(g\in D,\ \ell\ge5\text{ prime}).\quad} \end{equation} For a fixed $g$, the same equivalence holds pointwise. This is a reformulation of the remaining tame quartic gate; it does not assert the identities in \eqref{eq:tame-harmonic-2}.

label: prop:ns-lns-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Use the compatible standard markings of Nakamura--Schneps \cite[Theorem 11.2]{NS2000} and Lochak--Nakamura--Schneps \cite[Theorem 1.1]{LNS}. For $F=(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$, write $\rho=\rho_2(F)$ and \[ w_1=1,\qquad w_j=(a_1\cdots a_{j-1})^j\quad(2\leq j\leq2g), \qquad K_F=\prod_{j=2}^{2g}w_j^{\,(-1)^{j+1}4\rho}. \] Let $A_F^{\mathrm{NS2000}}$ denote the standard quilt representative and $A_F^{\mathrm{LNS}}$ the representative given by the explicit chain formulas. On each of $\widehat\Gamma_{g,0}$ and $\widehat\Gamma_{g,1}$ one has \[ A_F^{\mathrm{NS2000}}=\operatorname{Ad}(K_F)\circ A_F^{\mathrm{LNS}}. \] In particular the two outer actions are equal. If $\rho_2(F)=0$, these standard representatives themselves are equal.

label: prop:nonunique-stabilizer-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\sigma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{g-1}\}$ be a cut system with connected complement, and let $H$ be its oriented stabilizer in the full profinite pure mapping class group. Let $H_i$ be the oriented stabilizer of $\sigma\setminus\{\gamma_i\}$. The identity of $H$ has more than one inertia-preserving extension to $H_i$.

label: prop:degeneracy-two
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $F=(1,f)$ be a normalized element of $\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$. Let $\Phi_F$ be its standard action on $\widehat B$, so that \[ \Phi_F(u)=u,\qquad \Phi_F(v)=q^{-1}vq,\qquad q=f(u^2,v^2). \] Then $\Phi_F$ preserves the closure of $\Gamma_0(2)$, and its restriction commutes with both degeneracy maps to $\widehat B$.

label: prop:local-brauer-frame
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(T,W)\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_3)^2: \operatorname{tr}(T)\operatorname{tr}(W^2)\in\mathbb Z_3^\times\}. \] On this domain define \[ \mathfrak b(T,W)= \big[(\operatorname{tr}(T)\operatorname{tr}(W^2),3)_{\mathbb Q_3}\big] \in\operatorname{Br}(\mathbb Q_3)[2]. \] Here brackets denote a quaternion algebra's Brauer class. This invariant is unchanged by independent conjugation of $T$ and $W$. Suppose their reductions have the form \[ \bar T\in(-I)^{\epsilon_3}\langle R_0\rangle, \qquad \bar W\in S_0^{\epsilon_2}\langle-I\rangle, \] where $R_0$ is the standard nonidentity unipotent matrix of order three in $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3)$ and $S_0^2=-I$. Then $(T,W)\in\mathcal D$ and \[ \mathfrak b(T,W)=(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3) [(-1,-3)_{\mathbb Q_3}]. \] Its local Hilbert sign is $(-1)^{\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3}$.

label: prop:quartic-conductor
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The extension $L/K$ is cyclic of degree four. Its two faithful finite-order Hecke characters are $\psi,\psi^{-1}$ and \[ \mathfrak f(\psi)=\mathfrak f(\psi^{-1})=\mathfrak p^6, \qquad \mathfrak f(\psi^2)=\mathfrak p^4. \] All three characters have trivial infinity type. The absolute discriminant of $L$ is $2^{24}$. The representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{G_K}^{G_{\mathbb Q}}\psi$ is odd and irreducible of dimension two, has conductor $256$, and has determinant $\chi_{-4}$.

label: thm:uniform-odd-arithmetic-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, the coefficient \[ m_{2r+1}(g)=[S^{2r}T]f_g\qquad(g\in C_{r-1}) \] is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, with \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(J(C_{r-1})) =2^{2r+1}\mathbf Z_2. \] Its kernel is $C_r$. In particular each inclusion $C_r\subset C_{r-1}$ is proper, all these subgroups are closed and normal in $G$, and \[ G=C_rH\quad(r\ge0),\qquad G=C_\infty H. \] Moreover \[ C_\infty=\{g\in D:B_g(X,Y)=1\},\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] Here $B_g$ is its dyadic power-series component; no assertion about other components of the adelic beta function is made.

label: prop:uniform-odd-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $s\ge0$, the kernel of restriction \[ H^1(C_s,\mathbf F_2)^G\longrightarrow H^1(C_\infty,\mathbf F_2)^G \] is the one-dimensional space generated by \[ \zeta_s(g)=m_{2s+3}(g)/2^{2s+3}\pmod2. \] For the original normalized group $N$, the kernel of restriction to $C_\infty$ is \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] Each of these kernels has injective restriction to the corresponding arithmetic subgroup.

label: cor:dyadic-metabelian-deep-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \[ E=C_\infty\cap D_{10},\qquad J_E=E\cap H. \] Then $E$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $D_{10}$ and of infinite index there, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E]J_E}. \] Every pro-$2$ Magnus word on $E$ starts in degree at least eleven, and its dyadic beta multiplier is identically one. The kernel of restriction from $H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $H^1(E,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \]

label: thm:weight-eight-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every word belonging to $D_7$ starts in degree eight. Its homogeneous part of degree eight lies in a primitive rank-one integral Lie module, and \[ m_8(D_7)=m_8(J_7)=\mathbf Z_2. \] Set $D_8=D_7\cap\ker m_8$ and $J_8=D_8\cap H$. Then $D_8$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, \[ D_7=D_8J_7,\qquad G=D_8H,\qquad B\simeq D_8/\overline{[G,D_8]J_8}. \] Every word belonging to $D_8$ starts in degree at least nine. The continuous character $\eta_8=m_8\bmod2$ is $G$-invariant on $D_7$ and has nonzero arithmetic restriction. It has no $G$-invariant extension to $D$ or to $N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2)$.

label: lem:weight-eight-leading-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose $f\in\gamma_8$ satisfies the two-cycle and three-cycle relations \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Then its homogeneous part of degree eight is \[ \operatorname{in}_8(f)=b\mathcal L_8\quad\text{for a unique }b\in\mathbf Z_2. \] If $h_w$ denotes a degree-eight Lyndon coordinate, then $b=-h_{SSSTSSTT}$ and $m_8(f)=7b$.

label: lem:weight-eight-arithmetic-commutator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has $\overline{[M,M]}\subseteq D_7$. There are $\sigma\in H\cap M$ and $h\in H$ such that, with $s=h\sigma h^{-1}$, \[ w_8=[\sigma,s]\in J_7, \qquad m_8(w_8)=63\,m_3(\sigma)\,\tau_5(\sigma) \in\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] Moreover $w_8=[\sigma,k]$ for some $k\in D\cap H$.

label: cor:weight-eight-original-character-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $E$ be any closed $G$-stable subgroup containing $D$ and contained in $M$, and let $A$ be a finite abelian group with trivial $G$-action. Then \[ \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(E,A)^G: \chi(D_8)=0\} = \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(E,A)^G: \chi(D_7)=0\}. \] In particular, \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\mathbf F_2)\right) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \]

label: thm:eleven-mixed-mixed-reduction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The coordinate \[ b_{11}(g)=[S^6TST^3]f_g\qquad(g\in E) \] is a continuous additive homomorphism satisfying \[ b_{11}(aga^{-1})=\lambda_2(a)^{11}b_{11}(g) \quad(a\in G,\ g\in E). \] Its full and arithmetic images are both saturated: \[ b_{11}(E)=b_{11}(J(E))=\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently \[ E'=\ker(b_{11}|_E) \] is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, and \[ E/E'\simeq\mathbf Z_2,\qquad G=E'H, \qquad B\simeq E'/\overline{[G,E'](E'\cap H)}. \] For $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$, its restriction kernel remains \[ \ker\bigl(X_2\longrightarrow H^1(E',\mathbf F_2)\bigr) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The invariant character $b_{11}\bmod2$ on $E$ is nonzero on $J(E)$ and has no $G$-invariant extension to $N$.

label: thm:weight-five-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The exact integral images are \[ m_5(D_3)=m_5(J_3)=32\mathbf Z_2. \] In particular, \[ \eta_5:D_3\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_5(g)=m_5(g)/32\pmod2, \] is a continuous $G$-invariant character with nonzero arithmetic restriction. The kernel of $m_5$, \[ D_5=D_3\cap\ker m_5, \qquad J_5=D_5\cap H=J_3\cap\ker m_5, \] is a proper closed normal subgroup satisfying \[ D_3=D_5J_3,\qquad G=D_5H. \] The relative abelian quotient refines canonically to \[ B\simeq D_3/\overline{[G,D_3]J_3} \simeq D_5/\overline{[G,D_5]J_5}. \]

label: lem:weight-five-coefficients
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose $f\in\gamma_5$ satisfies \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Put \[ a=[S^4T]f,\quad c_5=[STSTS]f,\quad c_7=[STSTSTS]f,\quad c_9=[STSTSTSTS]f. \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-five-three-coefficients} c_5=-2a,\qquad c_7\equiv5a\pmod{16},\qquad c_9\equiv2a\pmod4. \end{equation}

label: prop:weight-five-upper-bound
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in D_3$, one has $m_5(g)\in32\mathbf Z_2$.

label: lem:tau-five
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\tau_5$ is a continuous homomorphism on $\ker\lambda$, and \[ \tau_5(hzh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^5\tau_5(z) \qquad(h\in G,\ z\in\ker\lambda). \] On $D_3$, it is equal to $12m_5$.

label: prop:weight-five-arithmetic-generator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists $w\in J_3$ with $m_5(w)\in32\mathbf Z_2^\times$.

label: cor:weight-five-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_5$ does not extend to a $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-character of $D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and hence does not extend to one of $N$. Nevertheless $D_5$ is a strictly smaller normalization with the same relative abelian quotient. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly \[ \bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The kernel of restriction from $H^1(D,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly $\mathbf F_2\eta_3|_D$. For every odd prime $p$, restriction from $H^1(N,\mathbf F_p)^G$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_p)$ is injective.

label: prop:weight-nine-arithmetic-value
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is $w_9\in J_8$ such that \[ m_9(w_9)=512\cdot12746612385\,\tau_9(\sigma), \qquad \tau_9(\sigma)\in\mathbf Z_2^\times, \] where $\sigma$ is the arithmetic element used in the preceding normalizations. Thus $512\mathbf Z_2\subseteq m_9(J_8)$.

label: thm:weight-nine-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_9(D_8)=m_9(J_8)=512\mathbf Z_2. \] The same equality holds with $D_8,J_8$ replaced by $D_7,J_7$. For $D_9=D_8\cap\ker m_9$ and $J_9=D_9\cap H$, \[ D_8=D_9J_8,\qquad G=D_9H,\qquad B\simeq D_9/\overline{[G,D_9]J_9}. \] The subgroup $D_9$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$, and every word belonging to it starts in degree at least ten. Moreover, \[ (m_8,m_9):D_7\longrightarrow\mathbf Z_2\times512\mathbf Z_2 \] is surjective already on $J_7$ and has kernel $D_9$.

label: prop:eta-nine-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character \[ \eta_9:D_7\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2,\qquad \eta_9(g)=m_9(g)/512\pmod2 \] is continuous and $G$-invariant. Its restriction to $D_8$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction and has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_5$.

label: cor:weight-nine-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic-character kernels on restriction to $D_9$ are as follows: \[ \begin{array}{c|l} \text{domain}&\text{kernel}\\ \hline D_8&\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_7&\mathbf F_2\eta_8\oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_5&\mathbf F_2\eta_7\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_8\\ D_3&\mathbf F_2\eta_5\\ N&\displaystyle\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \end{array} \]

label: lem:weight-seven-matrix-filtration
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $Q$ be the closed subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_2)$ generated by $U^2,V^2$, where \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Let $\mathcal B_r$ be the principal congruence group modulo $2^r$, and let $\mathcal A_r$ consist of determinant-one matrices whose diagonal entries are $1$ modulo $2^r$ and whose off-diagonal entries are zero modulo $2^{r+1}$. Then \[ \gamma_{2k}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal A_{3k-1},\qquad \gamma_{2k+1}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{3k+1}\quad(k\ge1). \] In particular, $\gamma_7(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{10}$, $\gamma_9(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{13}$ and $\gamma_{10}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal A_{14}$.

label: thm:weight-seven-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_7(D_5)=m_7(J_5)=128\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently, for $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ and $J_7=D_7\cap H$, \[ D_5=D_7J_5,\qquad G=D_7H,\qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[G,D_7]J_7}. \] The subgroup $D_7$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$, and \[ \eta_7:D_5\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_7(g)=m_7(g)/128\pmod2 \] is a continuous $G$-invariant character with nonzero arithmetic restriction.

label: cor:weight-seven-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_7$ has no $G$-invariant continuous extension to $D_3$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. Moreover, writing $\psi_q=\rho_q^I/2\pmod2$ for the divided odd-prime Kummer characters on $N$, one still has \[ \ker\bigl[H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G\longrightarrow H^1(D_7,\mathbf F_2)\bigr] =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] On $D_3$, the corresponding kernel is exactly $\mathbf F_2\eta_5$.

label: thm:weight-seven-bounds
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every word belonging to $D_5$ has zero Magnus components below degree seven. The map $m_7:D_5\to\mathbf Z_2$ is a continuous homomorphism and \[ m_7(hgh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^7m_7(g) \qquad(h\in G,\ g\in D_5). \] Its arithmetic and full images are exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-image-interval} m_7(J_5)=m_7(D_5)=128\mathbf Z_2. \end{equation} The corresponding degree-seven Hall images both equal $8\mathbf Z_2\mathbf L$, where $\mathbf L$ is the primitive integral vector specified below.

label: lem:weight-seven-leading-spaces
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose that $f\in\gamma_5$ satisfies the two-cycle and three-cycle relations with multiplier one. Put $a=[S^4T]f$. Its Hall coordinates in degrees five and six are \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-lower-vector} a\left(1,-2,\tfrac32,2,\tfrac12,-1, -2,\tfrac72,-\tfrac32,-4,-\tfrac12,\tfrac32, \tfrac72,\tfrac32,-2\right). \end{equation} In particular, $a=0$ implies that $f$ starts in degree seven. If $f$ starts in degree seven and satisfies the same two relations, its degree-seven Hall vector has the form $a\mathbf v+b\mathbf w$, where $a=[S^6T]f$, $b$ is the sixth degree-seven Hall coordinate, and \begin{align} \mathbf v={}&\left(1,-3,5,5,-2,0,-12,-5,-2,\tfrac23, -5,5,8,3,-\tfrac{11}3,4,3,-1\right), \label{eq:weight-seven-v}\\ \mathbf w={}&\left(0,0,0,0,0,1,1,0,0,\tfrac13, -1,-1,-1,0,-\tfrac13,0,0,0\right). \label{eq:weight-seven-w} \end{align} These are necessary leading-term conditions; they assert no lifting of an arbitrary truncated solution to a profinite automorphism.

label: lem:weight-seven-integral-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For an element of $D_5$, the parameters in \eqref{eq:weight-seven-v}--\eqref{eq:weight-seven-w} satisfy \[ 16b=19a. \] Consequently $a\in16\mathbf Z_2$, and the integral leading line is generated by the primitive vector \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-primitive-vector} \mathbf L=(16,-48,80,80,-32,19,-173,-80,-32, 17,-99,61,109,48,-65,64,48,-16). \end{equation} The leading Hall vector of an element is $(a/16)\mathbf L$. Moreover, its leading alternating Magnus coefficient is $[STSTSTS]f=-2a$.

label: lem:weight-seven-beta
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\tau_7$ is a continuous homomorphism on $\ker\lambda$, with conjugation weight $\lambda_2^7$. On $D_5$ it equals $360m_7$.

label: prop:weight-seven-arithmetic-value
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is $z_5\in J_5$ with \[ m_7(z_5)\in128\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] More explicitly, it can be chosen so that $m_7(z_5)=128\cdot199017\,\tau_7(\sigma)$ for an arithmetic $\sigma$ with $\tau_7(\sigma)$ odd.

label: thm:weight-ten-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full and arithmetic images are \[ m_{10}(D_9)=m_{10}(J_9)=\mathbf Z_2. \] For $D_{10}=D_9\cap\ker m_{10}$ and $J_{10}=D_{10}\cap H$, \[ D_9=D_{10}J_9,\qquad G=D_{10}H,\qquad B\simeq D_{10}/\overline{[G,D_{10}]J_{10}}. \] The subgroup $D_{10}$ is proper, closed and normal, and its words start in degree at least eleven.

label: lem:weight-ten-leading-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every multiplier-one GT word starting in degree ten, the homogeneous term of degree ten is $A\mathcal L_{10}$ with $A\in\mathbf Z_2$. It vanishes exactly when $m_{10}$ vanishes.

label: lem:weight-ten-arithmetic-unit
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an arithmetic commutator $w_{10}\in J_9$ such that \[ m_{10}(w_{10})=-141\cdot729\,m_3(\sigma)\tau_7(\sigma) \in\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] Moreover $w_{10}=[\sigma,k]$ for some $k\in D\cap H$.

label: prop:eta-ten-extension-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant character $\eta_{10}=m_{10}\pmod2$ on $D_9$ extends invariantly to $D_8$ by \[ \alpha_{10}(1,f)=[S^5TST^3]f\pmod2, \] but has no invariant extension to $D$ or $N$. The original kernel is \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_{10},\mathbf F_2)\right) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The joint raw-coefficient map $(m_9,m_{10})$ on $D_8$ has image $512\mathbf Z_2\times\mathbf Z_2$ already on $J_8$, with kernel $D_{10}$. Its invariant quadratic-character kernel on restriction to $D_{10}$ is $\mathbf F_2\eta_9\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_{10}$.

label: thm:even-characters
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $p\geq5$ be prime, let $m\geq2$ be even, and put $h_m=\dim_\Q(W/[W,W])_m$. For every $k\geq1$ such that $(p-1)p^{k-1}$ divides $m$, there is a continuous surjection \[ \GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle} \longrightarrow(\Z/p^k\Z)^{h_m}. \] The map is already onto on the global multiplier-one subgroup of $\GTz$. In particular weight sixteen gives a quotient $(\Z/17\Z)^{38}$.

label: lem:realization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $p\geq5$, let $\mathcal U$ be the multiplier-one subgroup in the image of $\GTz$ on the free pro-$p$ group $P$ on $X,Y$. Let $\mathcal U_n$ consist of pairs whose normalized conjugator belongs to $\gamma_nP$. Then \[ \mathcal U_2=\mathcal U_3=\mathcal U, \qquad \mathcal U_n/\mathcal U_{n+1}\simeq W_n(\Z_p), \qquad [\mathcal U_i,\mathcal U_j]\subset\mathcal U_{i+j}. \] Every element of the local multiplier-one group has a full gentle lift of global multiplier one.

label: lem:compact-log
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $U$ be a closed subgroup of a unipotent matrix group over $\Q_p$. Set $L=\operatorname{span}_{\Q_p}\log U$. Then $L$ is a nilpotent Lie algebra and $U$ contains $\exp(J)$ for some full $\Z_p$-lattice $J\subset L$. These statements apply to every closed subgroup of $U$.

label: cor:all-orders
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $Q=\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}$. There is a continuous surjection \[ Q^{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}} \prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z. \] For every prime $p\geq5$, the vector space $\Hom_{\cts}(Q,\F_p)$ has dimension exactly $\aleph_0$.

label: lem:frame-all-multipliers-congruence
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in\mathcal G$ and every prime $\ell$ there is a unique matrix \[ D_{g,\ell}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{g,\ell}&b_{g,\ell}\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \] such that $\widetilde q_\ell\Phi_g=\operatorname{Ad}(D_{g,\ell})\widetilde q_\ell$. It depends continuously on $g$, and $D_{gh,\ell}=D_{g,\ell}D_{h,\ell}$. For $h\in N_0$, its reduction modulo twelve is the identity.

label: prop:frame-sign-conjugation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The restrictions of $a_2,a_3$, and hence $\delta$, to $N_0$ are invariant under conjugation by $\mathcal G$.

label: thm:global-frame-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a unique continuous character \[ \Delta:\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which restricts to $\delta$ on $N_0$ and is zero on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For any $g\in\mathcal G$, choose $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ with $(\lambda,\rho_2)(\sigma)=(\lambda,\rho_2)(g)$. Then \[ \Delta(g)=\delta(g\sigma^{-1}). \] This character vanishes on the full pentagon group.

label: thm:deep-frame-witness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a multiplier-one gentle element $e=(1,f)$ such that \[ f\in F''',\qquad \rho_2(e)=0. \] Its modular automorphism $\Phi$ fixes $\tau$ and induces the identity under $q$. Its unique pure torsion frames, defined by \[ \Phi(s)=\beta s\beta^{-1},\qquad \Phi(r)=ArA^{-1}, \] satisfy \[ q(\beta)=1,\qquad q(A)=\zeta. \] In particular $e$ acts identically on $F/F'''$, and every character factoring through its metabelian action vanishes on $e$.

label: cor:frame-character-nonzero
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\Delta$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:global-frame-character} is nonzero on $N_0$ and is outside the span of all continuous quadratic characters factoring through the metabelian action. In particular $\Delta$ and the characters $\vartheta_p$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:quadratic-beta-family} are linearly independent.

label: thm:peripheral-lifting
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a continuous automorphism of $\overline\Lambda$.
