Suppose that elements $\overline c_i\in\overline\Lambda$ satisfy \[ \alpha(\pi(x_i)) =\overline c_i\pi(x_i)\overline c_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] There are a continuous automorphism $\Phi$ of $\Lambda$ and elements $c_i\in\Lambda$ such that \[ \pi\Phi=\alpha\pi, \qquad \pi(c_i)=\overline c_i, \qquad \Phi(x_i)=c_ix_ic_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] If one specified conjugator $\overline c_i$ is the identity, the lift can be chosen so that the corresponding $c_i$ is the identity.

label: lem:finite-peripheral-refinement
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $q:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow E$ be a finite quotient, let $A\triangleleft E$, and write $D=E/A$ and $q_D=q\bmod A$. There are a finite central extension $\beta:D^\dagger\twoheadrightarrow D$ and an epimorphism $q^\dagger:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow D^\dagger$ such that $\beta q^\dagger=q_D$, with the following property. Suppose $q_1^\dagger:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow D^\dagger$ is an epimorphism and $r_i\in D^\dagger$ satisfy \[ q_1^\dagger(x_i)=r_iq^\dagger(x_i)r_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] There is an epimorphism $q_1:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow E$ and elements $C_i\in E$ with \[ q_1(x_i)=C_iq(x_i)C_i^{-1},\qquad C_i\bmod A=\beta(r_i),\qquad q_1\bmod A=\beta q_1^\dagger. \]

label: thm:weight16
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $k=\Q$ and for $k=\F_{17}$, \[ \dim_k W_{16}=75,\qquad \dim_k[W,W]_{16}=37,\qquad \dim_k(W/[W,W])_{16}=38. \] The bracket space has a basis consisting of thirty-seven brackets of homogeneous elements of weights less than sixteen.

label: thm:main-character-quotients
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $Q=\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}$. There is a continuous surjection \[ Q^{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow (\Z/2\Z)^{\mathbb N}\times \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}}\prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z, \] already onto on the global multiplier-one subgroup. For $p=2$ and for every prime $p\geq5$, the vector space $\Hom_{\cts}(Q,\F_p)$ has dimension $\aleph_0$.

label: thm:frame-overview
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a continuous character $\Delta:\GTz\to\F_2$ vanishing on $\GT$ and an element $e=(1,f)\in\GTz$ such that \[ \rho_2(e)=0,\qquad f\in\widehat F_2''',\qquad \Delta(e)=1. \] Consequently $\Delta$ is outside the span of the quadratic characters that factor through the metabelian action, including the beta characters constructed in this paper.

label: thm:main-pentagon17
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $\F_{17}$ the map $P_{16}$ has rank seventy and a five-dimensional kernel contained in $[W,W]_{16}$. Its restriction to that bracket space has rank thirty-two. Consequently \[ W_{16}/[W,W]_{16}\longrightarrow \mathfrak t_{4,16}/P_{16}([W,W]_{16}) \] is injective, of rank thirty-eight. Its dual injects linearly into the continuous $\F_{17}$-valued characters of the full gentle group which vanish on $\GT$, already after restriction to global multiplier one. Every nonzero functional gives a character of order seventeen.

label: prop:dual
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $B_n=[W,W]_n$ and $K_n=\ker P_n$. The linear functionals on $W_n$ that annihilate both brackets and linear pentagon solutions are \[ C_n=\Ann(B_n)\cap\im(P_n^*) =\bigl(W_n/(B_n+K_n)\bigr)^*. \] In particular $P_n$ is a map on $W_n/B_n$ only when $P_n(B_n)=0$.

label: prop:weight12
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The space $W_{12}$ has dimension seven and its bracket subspace has dimension six. For the integral basis specified in Section~\ref{sec:cert}, the primitive functional \[ \ell=(-4,1,8,-4,-17,14,84) \] annihilates both $[W,W]_{12}$ and $\ker P_{12}$ over $\Q$. It has the same properties after reduction modulo thirteen and is nonzero there. Consequently $C_{12}$ is one-dimensional over $\Q$ and $\F_{13}$.

label: lem:cover-sign-homology
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite set of primes congruent to five modulo twelve, and let \[ Q=\Gamma\Big/ \bigcap_{p\in\mathcal P}\overline{U_6'U_6^p}. \] Then $Q$ fits into a split exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}M_p \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow\Gamma_6\longrightarrow1, \] and $Q^{\mathrm{ab}}=C_6$. Choose a complement to its kernel. For $p\in\mathcal P$, let $\alpha_p$ act as $-1$ on $V_p$, and as the identity on $W_p$, on all $M_q$ with $q\ne p$, and on this complement. Then $\alpha_p$ is an involutive automorphism of $Q$. It acts trivially on $H_2(Q,\mathbb Z)$.

label: lem:sign-central-extensions
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $Q$ and $\alpha_p$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:cover-sign-homology}, and let $q:\Gamma\to Q$ be the natural quotient. Every finite central extension \[ 1\longrightarrow Z\longrightarrow D\longrightarrow Q \longrightarrow1 \] admits an involutive automorphism $\widetilde\alpha_p$ which lifts $\alpha_p$ and fixes $Z$ pointwise. For each $t\in\{s,r,\tau\}$, choose $b_t\in V_p$ such that \[ \alpha_p(q(t))=b_tq(t)b_t^{-1}. \] Such an element exists. For every lift $\widetilde t\in D$ of $q(t)$, there is a lift $\widetilde b_t\in D$ of $b_t$ with \[ \widetilde\alpha_p(\widetilde t) =\widetilde b_t\widetilde t\widetilde b_t^{-1}. \] The same assertions hold with $\tau^{-1}$ as the third peripheral.

label: thm:quadratic-sign-lifts
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every finite set $\mathcal P$ of primes congruent to five modulo twelve and each $p\in\mathcal P$, there is a full multiplier-one gentle element whose action on the sixth-root homology characters modulo each $q\in\mathcal P$ is $-1$ on $(\omega,\omega),(\omega^2,\omega^2)$ when $q=p$, and is the identity on all other nontrivial characters. One may at the same time prescribe identity conjugator values in any fixed finite quotient of $\Gamma$ of order divisible only by two and three.

label: lem:cover-unitarity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement:
Let $\phi$ be a continuous automorphism of $F$ inducing the identity on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ and preserving the three positive peripheral classes. On a nontrivial sixth-root character $(a,b)$ with \[ a
e1,\qquad b
e1,\qquad ab
e1, \] let $B_\phi(a,b)$ be the scalar by which it acts on the corresponding one-dimensional summand of $H_1(U_6,\overline{\mathbb F}_p)$, where $p\geq5$. Then \[ B_\phi(a,b)B_\phi(a^{-1},b^{-1})=1. \]

label: thm:quadratic-beta-family
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p\equiv5\pmod{12}$ there is a continuous character \[ \vartheta_p:\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which vanishes on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Their joint map is surjective, already on the multiplier-one subgroup: \[ (\vartheta_p)_p: \widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_{0,1} \twoheadrightarrow\prod_{p\equiv5\ (12)}\mathbb F_2. \] Consequently the continuous quadratic character space of the gentle group vanishing on the pentagon group, and also the one vanishing on $G_{\mathbb Q}$, has dimension $\aleph_0$.

label: cor:simultaneous-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a continuous surjection, already onto on global multiplier one, \[ \left(\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}\right)^{\mathrm{ab}} \longrightarrow (\Z/2\Z)^{\mathbb N}\times \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}} \prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z. \] Consequently its continuous character group with values in $\Q/\Z$ contains the direct sum of the dual finite cyclic groups displayed here.

label: thm:pentagon17
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $\F_{17}$ the pentagon map in weight sixteen has the following ranks: \[ \operatorname{rank}P_{16}=70,\qquad \dim\ker P_{16}=5,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(P_{16}|_{[W,W]_{16}})=32. \] Its kernel is contained in $[W,W]_{16}$. Consequently the induced map \[ W_{16}/[W,W]_{16}\longrightarrow \mathfrak t_{4,16}/P_{16}([W,W]_{16}) \] is injective and has rank thirty-eight. Every functional on $(W/[W,W])_{16}$ annihilates the linear pentagon kernel.

label: thm:topweight
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p\geq5$, put $m=p-1$. After a choice of tame splitting, there is an injective linear map \[ \bigl(W_m(\F_p)/([W,W]_m(\F_p)+\ker P_m)\bigr)^* \longrightarrow \Hom_{\cts}\bigl(\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}, \F_p\bigr). \] The character associated with $\ell$ restricts to $\ell$ on the leading weight-$m$ subgroup. The characters are independent already on the global multiplier-one subgroup. In particular the integral certificate in weight twelve gives a nonzero character of order thirteen without using the Deligne--Drinfeld theorem; Theorem~\ref{thm:pentagon17} realizes all thirty-eight weight-sixteen functionals as characters of order seventeen.

label: cor:quadratic-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\delta:\GTz\to\F_2$ be a continuous character. Its kernel contains a global multiplier-one element outside $\GT$. If $\delta$ is nonzero and vanishes on $\GT$, then \[ \GT\varsubsetneqq\ker\delta\varsubsetneqq\GTz. \] This conclusion does not use the Deligne--Drinfeld theorem.

label: prop:kn-linear-sign-model
status: Superseded by AQ.156; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There is an $\mathbb F_{17}$-linear automorphism of the space (H) that commutes with the whole deck group $A$, preserves its alternating intersection form, and has determinant $-1$ on the ten-dimensional $\omega$-eigenspace over $\mathbb F_{17^2}$. Its quadratic norm-one determinant sign is therefore $-1$. This is a linear model, not a GT element or a solution of the pentagon or of (K).

label: thm:main-uniform-dyadic-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.157; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $C_0=D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and \[ C_r=D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker c_{2j+1},\qquad C_\infty=\bigcap_{r\ge0}C_r. \] For every $r\ge1$, the coefficient $m_{2r+1}=[S^{2r}T]f$ is additive on $C_{r-1}$, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, and satisfies \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1}\cap H) =2^{2r+1}\Z_2,\qquad \ker(m_{2r+1}|_{C_{r-1}})=C_r. \] All these subgroups are closed and normal, and \[ G=C_rH=C_\infty H,\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] The subgroup $C_\infty$ is exactly the kernel in $D$ of the dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(C_\infty,\F_2)$ is the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. Finally, $E=C_\infty\cap D_{10}$ has infinite index in $D_{10}$, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E](E\cap H)}. \] Its elements have no pro-$2$ Magnus term below degree eleven and have trivial dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E,\F_2)$ is again exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:tame-harmonic-word-gate
status: Superseded by AQ.158; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For every $g\in D$ the corrected harmonic frame satisfies \[ W_g=f_g(U^2,S)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \tag{1} \] Consequently its residue belongs to the cyclic group \[ \mathcal T_\ell =\{aI+bS_\ell:a,b\in\mathbb F_\ell,\ a^2+b^2=1\}, \qquad |\mathcal T_\ell|=\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell). \] The simultaneous compatibility of the radical and CM actions on every rational quartic root is equivalent to the following family of finite word identities: \[ \boxed{\quad f_g(U_\ell^2,S_\ell)^{m_\ell}=I \qquad(g\in D,\ \ell\ge5\text{ prime}).\quad} \tag{2} \] For a fixed $g$, the same equivalence holds pointwise. This is a reformulation of the remaining tame quartic gate; it does not assert the identities in (2).

label: prop:two-relative-extensions
status: Superseded by AQ.146; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Each of $\epsilon_h,\epsilon_c$ has a unique extension to a continuous homomorphism $G\to\mathbb F_2$ that is zero on $H$. Their sum is the established residual relative character $\chi_3$. The harmonic extension is proved to vanish in Section~\ref{sec:harmonic-dyadic-comparison}; the cubic extension then equals $\chi_3$, whose vanishing remains open.

label: cor:harmonic-defect-zero
status: Superseded by AQ.147; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$, the finite harmonic frame sign satisfies $w=\eta$. Thus the previously constructed relative character $\epsilon_h=w+\eta$ is zero on the whole of full GT, and the remaining exceptional character is $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$. No vanishing of $\epsilon_c$ is asserted.

label: thm:main-harmonic-dyadic
status: Superseded by AQ.151; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_2(g)=0$, the pure harmonic frame satisfies \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uvu) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $w_3=\eta$ on $D$, the relative character $\epsilon_h$ is zero, and $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau_3+\eta$. The vanishing of this remaining cubic comparison character is not determined.

label: thm:main-weight-ten-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.142; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: On $D_9$, put $m_{10}(g)=[S^5TST^3]f_g$ and $J_9=D_9\cap H$. This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{10}$, with \[ m_{10}(D_9)=m_{10}(J_9)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_{10}$ is proper, closed and normal, and \[ \GT=D_{10}H,\qquad B\simeq D_{10}/\overline{[\GT,D_{10}](D_{10}\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_{10}$ starts in Magnus degree at least eleven. The invariant character $\eta_{10}=m_{10}\pmod2$ extends invariantly to $D_8$, but not to $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_{10},\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-weight-seven-alternative
status: Superseded by AQ.129; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $D_5=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}$ and $J_5=D_5\cap H$. Every $g\in D_5$ starts in Magnus degree seven, and $m_7(g)=[S^6T]f_g$ is an additive weight-seven coordinate with \[ m_7(D_5)=m_7(J_5)=128\Z_2. \] The proper closed normal subgroup $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ satisfies \[ \GT=D_7H,\qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[\GT,D_7](D_7\cap H)}. \] The invariant character $\eta_7=m_7/128\pmod2$ on $D_5$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction. It has no invariant extension to $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_7,\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:main-weight-nine-bounds
status: Superseded by AQ.130; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $J_8=D_8\cap H$ and $m_9(g)=[S^8T]f_g$ for $g\in D_8$. This is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^9$, and \[ 512\Z_2\subseteq m_9(J_8)\subseteq m_9(D_8)\subseteq256\Z_2. \] Write $m_9(D_8)=2^e\Z_2$ and $m_9(J_8)=2^f\Z_2$; then $8\le e\le f\le9$. If $e<f$, the reduction of $m_9/2^e$ gives a nonzero continuous quadratic character of $\GT$ trivial on $H$. If $e=f$, its integral kernel $D_9$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, $\GT=D_9H$, the relative quotient $B$ is unchanged, and every $D_9$ word starts in degree at least ten. The proposition does not determine which alternative holds.

label: prop:weight-nine-upper256
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: One has \[ m_9(D_8)\subseteq256\mathbf Z_2. \] Together with the arithmetic value, this leaves a factor of two in each possible image.

label: cor:cubic-radical-joint-image
status: Superseded by AQ.127; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\widehat{\mathbf Z}\right) \times8\mathbf Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)) \] is surjective on $K=N\cap H$, with kernel $D_3$. Consequently the $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-characters of $N$ which vanish on $D_3$ form exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero $G$-invariant $\mathbf F_p$-character of $N$ vanishes on $D_3$.

label: prop:weight-nine-upper256
status: Superseded by AQ.128; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The upper bound improves to \[ m_9(D_8)\subseteq256\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently the image exponents in the preceding alternative satisfy $8\le e\le f\le9$. The remaining question is a factor of two.

label: thm:abelian-splitting
status: Superseded by AQ.117; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of profinite abelian groups \[ G^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq U\times B \] under which the multiplier is the first projection. Moreover \[ D=N\cap\overline{[G,G]},\qquad B\simeq\bigl(G/\overline{\langle\!\langle H\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr)^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p=H^1(N,\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad r_p:X_p\longrightarrow H^1(K,\mathbb F_p). \] Restriction gives canonical identifications \begin{align*} \ker r_p&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p),\\ H^1(G,\mathbb F_p)&\simeq \lambda^*H^1(U,\mathbb F_p)\oplus\ker r_p. \end{align*} Consequently $\ker r_p=0$ if and only if every continuous $\mathbb F_p$-character of $G$ factors through the multiplier. The multiplier identifies $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $U$ if and only if $N\subset\overline{[G,G]}$, and this holds if and only if $\ker r_p=0$ for every prime~$p$.

label: prop:two-relative-extensions
status: Superseded by AQ.120; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Each of $\epsilon_h,\epsilon_c$ has a unique extension to a continuous homomorphism $G\to\mathbb F_2$ that is zero on $H$. Their sum is the established residual relative character $\chi_3$. This statement asserts neither the vanishing nor the nonvanishing of either extension.

label: thm:main-weight-eight-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.125; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Every $g\in D_7$ has Magnus expansion starting in degree at least eight. Put \[ m_8(g)=[S^4TST^2]f_g,\qquad J_7=D_7\cap H. \] This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^8$, and \[ m_8(D_7)=m_8(J_7)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_8$ is proper, closed and normal in $\GT$, satisfies $\GT=D_8H$, and gives \[ B\simeq D_8/\overline{[\GT,D_8](D_8\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_8$ starts in Magnus degree at least nine. The invariant quadratic character $\eta_8=m_8\pmod2$ on $D_7$ has no invariant extension to $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. It does extend invariantly to $D_5$ by the same raw coefficient modulo two. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_8,\F_2)$ remains exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:eta-eight-extension-d5
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: The character $\eta_8$ on $D_7$ has a continuous $G$-invariant extension to $D_5$, given by \[ \widetilde\eta_8(1,f)=[S^4TST^2]f\pmod2. \] This does not assert an extension to $D_3$.

label: prop:main-weight-nine-bounds
status: Superseded by AQ.115; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $J_8=D_8\cap H$ and $m_9(g)=[S^8T]f_g$ for $g\in D_8$. This is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^9$, and \[ 512\Z_2\subseteq m_9(J_8)\subseteq m_9(D_8)\subseteq64\Z_2. \] Write $m_9(D_8)=2^e\Z_2$ and $m_9(J_8)=2^f\Z_2$; then $6\le e\le f\le9$. If $e<f$, the reduction of $m_9/2^e$ gives a nonzero continuous quadratic character of $\GT$ trivial on $H$. If $e=f$, its integral kernel $D_9$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, $\GT=D_9H$, the relative quotient $B$ is unchanged, and every $D_9$ word starts in degree at least ten. The proposition does not determine which alternative holds.

label: thm:main-weight-seven-alternative
status: Superseded by AQ.089; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $D_5=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}$ and $J_5=D_5\cap H$. Every $g\in D_5$ starts in Magnus degree seven, and $m_7(g)=[S^6T]f_g$ is an additive weight-seven coordinate. One has \[ 128\Z_2\subseteq m_7(J_5)\subseteq m_7(D_5)\subseteq64\Z_2. \] Write these two nonzero closed images as $m_7(D_5)=2^e\Z_2$, $m_7(J_5)=2^f\Z_2$. Then $6\le e\le f\le7$. If $(e,f)=(6,7)$, the character $m_7/64\pmod2$ gives a nonzero element of $\Hom(B,\F_2)$. In each of the other two cases, the proper closed normal subgroup $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ satisfies $\GT=D_7H$ and has the same relative abelian quotient $B$.

label: thm:weight-seven-bounds
status: Superseded by AQ.093; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Every word belonging to $D_5$ has zero Magnus components below degree seven. The map $m_7:D_5\to\mathbf Z_2$ is a continuous homomorphism and \[ m_7(hgh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^7m_7(g) \qquad(h\in G,\ g\in D_5). \] Its arithmetic and full images satisfy \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-image-interval} 128\mathbf Z_2\subseteq m_7(J_5) \subseteq m_7(D_5)\subseteq64\mathbf Z_2. \end{equation} The leading degree-seven images are nonzero closed rank-one $\mathbf Z_2$-modules on the explicit primitive line described below. In particular, there are uniquely determined integers \[ 6\le e\le f\le7, \qquad m_7(D_5)=2^e\mathbf Z_2, \qquad m_7(J_5)=2^f\mathbf Z_2. \] The equality of both images with $128\mathbf Z_2$ is not established by these bounds.

label: cor:weight-seven-relative-alternative
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Let $e,f$ be the exponents in Theorem~\ref{thm:weight-seven-bounds}, and put $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ and $J_7=D_7\cap H$. The subgroup $D_7$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$. Exactly one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item If $e<f$, the character \[ D_5\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad g\longmapsto m_7(g)/2^e\pmod2 \] is nonzero, $G$-invariant and zero on $J_5$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathbf F_2)\ne0$. \item If $e=f$, then \[ D_5=D_7J_5,\qquad G=D_7H, \qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[G,D_7]J_7}. \] Thus the kernel of $m_7$ gives the next proper arithmetic normalization. \end{enumerate} The interval bounds alone do not decide between these cases.

label: prop:weight-seven-upper64
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: One has \[ 128\mathbf Z_2\subseteq m_7(J_5) \subseteq m_7(D_5)\subseteq64\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently the two exponents in Corollary~\ref{cor:weight-seven-relative-alternative} satisfy $6\le e\le f\le7$. The only possible strict pair is $(e,f)=(6,7)$.

label: thm:main-cubic-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.069; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For $g=(1,f)$ put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f$ in the Magnus expansion $x=1+S$, $y=1+T$. Then \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\Z_2,\qquad m_3(N_{\mathrm{rad}})=m_3(G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}})=8\Z_2. \] Thus $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ belongs to $X_2$, and its restriction to $G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}$ is nonzero. It is linearly independent of the entire rational Kummer subspace. The joint map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh\right)\times8\Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto\bigl((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)\bigr) \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\ker m_3$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and of $\GT$, and \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad},3},\F_2)$ is precisely \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\F_2\eta_3. \] On $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$ put $m_5(g)=[S^4T]f$ and $K_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ$. Then \[ m_5(N_{\mathrm{rad},3})=m_5(K_{\mathrm{rad},3})=32\Z_2. \] Thus $N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\ker m_5$ is again proper and closed normal, with \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\cap\GQ)}. \]

label: prop:divided-multiplicative-defects
status: Construction remains valid; superseded as a GT candidate by Enriquez Theorem8.1 and Remark8.6, which force every displayed defect to be zero on GT
statement: For positive integers $a,b$, the divided difference \[ \delta_{a,b} =\frac{\rho_{ab}^I|_N-\rho_a^I|_N-\rho_b^I|_N}{2}\bmod2 \] belongs to $\ker r_2$. Its unique extension to a character of $G$ vanishing on $H$ is \[ \widetilde\delta_{a,b} =\frac{\rho_{ab}^I-\rho_a^I-\rho_b^I}{2}\bmod2. \] The numerator in the second expression takes values in $2\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ on the whole gentle group, so the same expression defines a character there which vanishes on $G_{\mathbb Q}$.
